edges.effect_quant: Updated syntheses continue to show higher Parkinson's risk in workers with occupational pesticide exposure, though exact estimates depend on how exposure is measured.
edges.mechanism: Many pesticide classes can plausibly injure dopaminergic pathways through mitochondrial stress, oxidative injury, and chronic neuroinflammation. That mechanistic plausibility helps explain why the association with Parkinson's disease keeps resurfacing across occupational evidence reviews.
edges.summary: The latest systematic review and meta-analysis again found a positive association between pesticide exposure and Parkinson's disease. Other occupational meta-analyses did not erase that signal; instead, they showed that the effect size shifts depending on whether exposure is measured broadly, by job title, or by more detailed pesticide-assessment methods.
edges.caveats: This edge pools many pesticide classes together, so it should not be read as proof that every pesticide carries the same neurologic risk. Recall bias and exposure misclassification remain major limitations, but the direction of association is more stable than the exact magnitude.
